description.narrative: (Yemen): Yemen faces one of the world's most severe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) crises. Inadequate WASH access fuels the spread of cholera and diarrhea, worsening malnutrition in a country with high levels of food insecurity and stunting, while also complicating efforts to control other communicable diseases. Females are particularly affected due to their traditional roles in fetching water, cooking, childcare, and caring for the sick and elderly. They are also at increased risk of gender-based violence when forced to seek private areas to use the bathroom after dark. Addressing extreme water scarcity is critical to limiting the spread of communicable diseases in an already fragile context..With FY 2024 funds, the activity will enhance sustainable access to safe water and sanitation, mitigating the impact of communicable diseases on vulnerable Yemenis in conflict-affected areas. Funding will support the rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools, encouraging children and youth to remain in school and reducing the risk of early marriage or recruitment into armed groups. School interventions will also provide facilities that accommodate people with disabilities, helping eliminate bias and stigma while ensuring equal access for all..The project will rehabilitate water and sanitation networks, improving service delivery to the most vulnerable communities. These interventions will focus on internally displaced person communities addressing issues like overflowing sewage systems. Hygiene awareness training will remain an integral part of the program, promoting better health outcomes. Additionally, funds will be used to strengthen the capacity of local water authorities to manage WASH facilities by providing them with essential tools to maintain facilities beyond U.S. Government investments. Most importantly, the program goes beyond service delivery by addressing issues related to safety, security, dignity, and community climate resilience....
